pairs.subject: machine-paced-delivery
pairs.evidence: src/features/agents/components/matrix/useLifecycle.ts:2 Here "build" means putting together a persona's runtime config from a build session (draft, tool test, promote to a live persona). No repository change, CI run, merge gate or delivery credential passes through this context. A search of src/features/agents/components/matrix found zero hits for 'pull request', 'pipeline', 'lefthook', 'ci.yml' and 'workflow_run'. The only 'commit'/'merge'/'github' hits are a code comment, an object-merge comment and connector test fixtures.

techniques.evidence: src/features/agents/components/matrix/useLifecycle.ts:11 Promote writes a persona row through IPC. It is not a machine-authored repository change reaching a merge gate, so the proposal contract has nothing to govern.
src/features/agents/components/matrix/useLifecycle.ts:5 This tests a persona's tools against live APIs. It does not run the repo's declared checks before a commit.
src/features/agents/components/matrix/useBuild.ts:2 Build state goes to a React UI. There is no checker output for an agent to diagnose.

pairs.registryProposal: This context has a delivery-shaped flow outside source control: an LLM writes a persona draft, a test gate runs (with the result held as 'unverified' when tools were skipped), and a human promotes it, with a force 'Approve Anyway' bypass (useLifecycle.ts:278-282). The rubber-stamp risk that human-gate-capacity describes applies to this kind of artifact promotion too. Consider noting in the golden path whether agent-authored non-code artifacts that move from draft to production fall in scope here or under hitl-approval.
